title: Democracy in Society
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 5 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Use a class vote for both types: a show of hands on a trip (direct) and electing a class monitor who then decides (representative).

skills.key_step: The child tells direct democracy (people decide themselves) from representative democracy (people elect leaders to decide) and does not call rule by one person democracy.

floor.prerequisite: Knows the arms of government and who sits in Parliament.
floor.question: Who are the members of the National Assembly?

steps: Ask: did the people decide themselves?
If yes, it is direct; if they chose someone, representative.
If one person decides alone, it is not democracy.
contexts: a class voting on a trip
a referendum on a new constitution

board.do: Draw two columns: direct and representative.

board.say: Electing an MP who makes laws for us goes where?

misconceptions.ask: The class votes by raising hands to choose a game. What type of democracy is this?
misconceptions.repair: Ask: did each person decide, or did chosen people decide for them?

listen_for: A leader who rules for life without elections
misconceptions.repair: Ask who chose the leader and who can remove him.

misconceptions.ask: In a referendum all voters decide on a law themselves. What type of democracy is this?
misconceptions.repair: Compare: electing an MP (someone decides for you) and a referendum (you decide).

misconceptions.ask: Is speaking at a public meeting about a new road part of democracy?
misconceptions.repair: List other ways people take part: meetings, petitions, peaceful protest.

checks.question: In which type of democracy do people elect leaders to decide for them?
A class votes with a show of hands on where to go for a trip. Which type is this?

skills.key_step: The child gives benefits of democracy and the fair way to practise it (free choice, secret ballot, same rules, accepting the result, respecting the minority).

floor.question: Electing a class monitor is which type of democracy?

steps: Ask: is the choice free and the rule the same for all?
Say what happens after the vote.
contexts: a losing candidate congratulating the winner

board.do: Write: "A candidate gives sweets for votes."
Wait for no and the reason.
Write the fair way: campaign with ideas.

misconceptions.ask: After the vote, 12 learners chose football and 8 chose netball. What is fair?
misconceptions.repair: Ask how the 8 can still get a turn another day.

misconceptions.ask: What is the fair way to choose a class monitor?
misconceptions.repair: Run a mock election with secret ballots.

misconceptions.ask: A candidate gives voters money for their votes. Is this fair?
misconceptions.repair: Ask whether people would vote for the best leader or for the money.

misconceptions.ask: A candidate lost. What is the fair way to respond?
misconceptions.repair: Discuss the peaceful ways to complain: courts, the electoral body.

checks.question: Give two benefits of democracy.
checks.answer: any two of: everyone has a voice, leaders answer to people, peaceful change, fair decisions

checks.question: Why is a secret ballot used?
checks.answer: So each voter chooses freely without fear
